name: Stanley Martinez
bio: Stanley Martinez is a founding member and currently serves as Chairman of the Board for the Submariners’ Advocacy Group (SAG), helping lead the organization’s mission to advocate for U.S. Navy Submariners, veterans, and their families. As one of SAG’s founding leaders, Stanley has played a central role in helping shape the organization’s strategic direction, outreach efforts, and growing national advocacy presence within the veteran and submarine communities.

A proud supporter of the Silent Service community, Stanley has dedicated himself to increasing awareness surrounding the unique operational demands and long-term health concerns associated with submarine duty. He remains deeply committed to educating current and former Submariners about the potential impacts of toxic exposures, radiation, and other unseen hazards associated with service beneath the sea, while advocating for improved awareness, recognition, and support for affected veterans.

In addition to his leadership role within SAG, Stanley has maintained a long and distinguished record of service and advocacy within the Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW). In the state of Utah, he served as State Commander from 2017 to 2018 and later served on the VFW National Legislative Committee from 2020 through 2024. His leadership within the veteran community reflects a continued commitment to supporting veterans at both the state and national levels.

Stanley is a Gold Legacy Life Member of the Veterans of Foreign Wars and the VFW National Home. He is also a Life Member of the Disabled American Veterans (DAV), Fleet Reserve Association (FRA), and the American Legion.
Further reflecting his commitment to national service, Stanley currently serves as a Presidential Appointee and lifetime board member for the United States Selective Service System.

Stanley holds a bachelor’s degree in Medical Management and continues to dedicate his time and leadership toward advancing veteran advocacy, organizational growth, and support for the Submarine Force community.

name: David Bozarth
bio: David Bozarth is a founding member and currently serves as President and Executive Director of the Submariners’ Advocacy Group (SAG), where he leads the organization’s national advocacy efforts on behalf of U.S. Navy Submariners, veterans, and their families. As one of SAG’s principal founders, David has played a central role in shaping the organization’s mission, strategic direction, and growing national presence within the veteran advocacy community.

Raised in a small rural town in Missouri, David developed a strong sense of patriotism, service, and duty from an early age. He enlisted in the United States Navy in 1978 and soon volunteered for submarine duty, beginning his journey into the Silent Service. After graduating at the top of his class from Basic Enlisted Submarine School in Groton, Connecticut, he completed follow-on technical training through Polaris Electronics “A” School and advanced Fire Control Technician “C” School training for the Poseidon Weapons System.

David subsequently reported aboard USS LEWIS AND CLARK (SSBN 644) (GOLD Crew), where he earned his Qualified in Submarines designation in February 1981. During his assignment aboard LEWIS AND CLARK, he qualified as a Missile Control Center Technician, Nuclear Weapons Security Guard, and Missile Control Center Supervisor. His operational experience included multiple strategic deterrent patrols, operational testing of the Poseidon Missile System, and participation in an extended refueling overhaul and post-shipyard recertification process supporting the nation’s strategic nuclear deterrence mission.

Following his honorable discharge from the United States Navy in 1984, David transitioned into the civilian sector, applying the technical expertise and operational discipline developed during his submarine service to careers supporting Department of the Navy and United States Marine Corps electronic security systems, information technology, information security, and project management initiatives. Throughout his civilian career, he has supported complex global information systems while continuing to dedicate time and expertise to nonprofit and veteran-service organizations.

David is also a Life Member of the Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW), where he has served in multiple leadership positions, including District Commander. Under his leadership, Missouri VFW District 7 achieved All-American status in 2022, 2023, and 2025. He has consistently utilized his leadership platform to advocate for greater awareness, visibility, and recognition of the service and sacrifices of Submariners and veterans of the Silent Service.

In March 2024, David recognized the growing need to advocate for Submariners affected by long-term toxic exposure concerns associated with the closed-loop atmosphere aboard U.S. Navy submarines. Following extensive research and collaboration with fellow Submarine veterans, he spearheaded the formation of the Submariners’ Advocacy Group in April 2024 alongside a team of fellow Submariners committed to advancing awareness and advocacy for the undersea warfare community.

Under David’s leadership as Executive Director, SAG has experienced rapid organizational growth and has become an increasingly recognized voice advocating for Submariners nationwide. His leadership, passion, and unwavering commitment to the Silent Service continue to drive SAG’s mission to support, educate, and advocate for those who have served beneath the sea.

name: Scott Muranko
bio: Scott Muranko serves on the Board of Directors for the Submariners’ Advocacy Group (SAG) as Secretary of the Board and Director of Governance. A retired U.S. Navy Senior Chief Yeoman (Submarines), Scott brings more than two decades of submarine service and over twenty years of leadership experience in manufacturing operations, workforce development, and technical training to the organization’s mission of advocating for U.S. Navy Submariners and their families.

Born and raised in Sterling, Virginia, Scott entered the United States Navy shortly after graduating high school with the intention of becoming a nuclear power operator. When a diagnosis of color blindness redirected his career path, he adapted without hesitation—transitioning into the Yeoman rating before volunteering for submarine duty and beginning what would become a distinguished twenty-year career in the Silent Service.

After completing Basic Enlisted Submarine School in January 1986, Scott reported aboard USS LEWIS AND CLARK (SSBN 644) (BLUE Crew) in Charleston, South Carolina. He earned his Qualified in Submarines designation during his second deterrent patrol and completed eight strategic deterrent patrols before transferring ashore as a Yeoman Second Class (Submarines).

Scott’s first shore assignment was with Navy Nuclear Field “A” School in Orlando, Florida, where he advanced to Yeoman First Class (Submarines). Eager to return to sea duty, he volunteered for assignment aboard USS WEST VIRGINIA (SSBN 736) (GOLD Crew) in Kings Bay, Georgia, serving as Leading Yeoman and earning selection to Chief Petty Officer following his fifth patrol with the crew.

He later served on the staff of Commander, Submarine Group Ten in Kings Bay, Georgia, where he helped oversee administrative and personnel support operations for multiple submarine crews and shore commands. Scott subsequently returned to sea aboard USS LOUISIANA (SSBN 743) (BLUE Crew), participating in the crew’s first five strategic deterrent patrols and advancing to Senior Chief Petty Officer.

Scott concluded his Navy career with Navy Recruiting District Denver, where his leadership contributed to the command being recognized as the top recruiting district in the nation for three consecutive years. Following twenty years of honorable and distinguished naval service, he retired from active duty and transferred to the Fleet Reserve.

Following his military retirement, Scott transitioned into the manufacturing and automotive sectors, building a second career focused on operational excellence, technical workforce development, and organizational training leadership. His civilian leadership experience includes positions with Coors, Lucid Motors, Carvana, and Ball Corporation. Throughout his post-Navy career, he has led large-scale technical training initiatives, building workforce development programs, and supported global manufacturing operations across multiple industries.

Since joining the SAG Board of Directors in 2025, Scott has played a central role in organizational governance modernization, board development, strategic communications, and advocacy initiatives focused on the long-term health impacts associated with submarine service. He also contributed to the development of The Unseen Burden: Toxic Exposures and Health Impacts on U.S. Navy Submariners, a landmark report examining the hidden health consequences associated with prolonged exposure to the closed-loop atmosphere aboard U.S. Navy submarines.
Scott currently resides in Phoenix, Arizona, with his wife, Melissa.

name: Chuck Sanders
bio: Charles “Chuck” Sanders serves in a leadership role within the Submariners’ Advocacy Group (SAG), supporting the organization’s mission to advocate for U.S. Navy Submariners, veterans, and their families. A proud member of the Silent Service community, Chuck brings decades of technical expertise, operational experience, and continued dedication to supporting fellow veterans and Submariners.

During his naval career, Chuck served in the United States Navy Submarine Force, where he developed the technical discipline, operational focus, and mission-oriented mindset that would continue to define both his military and civilian careers. His time within the Silent Service reinforced the values of professionalism, accountability, teamwork, and service that remain central to his work today.

Following his military service, Chuck built an extensive civilian career centered on advanced electronics, telecommunications, and network infrastructure systems. From 1991 through 2001, he served as a Senior Electronic Engineering Technician with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) in the Alaska Region, supporting critical technical and communications infrastructure in one of the nation’s most demanding operational environments.

Chuck later continued his technical and public service career with the State of Missouri Department of Higher Education and Workforce Development, where he served from 2002 through 2024 as both a Senior Telecommunications Technician and Senior Network Infrastructure Technician. Throughout this career, he supported complex communications and network systems while contributing to the operational reliability and technological infrastructure supporting higher education and workforce development initiatives across the state.

Chuck’s combined background in submarine operations, advanced technical systems, telecommunications, and public-sector infrastructure support provides valuable perspective within SAG’s leadership team. His experience reflects a lifelong commitment to disciplined service, technical excellence, and supporting both the veteran and Submarine communities.

Within SAG, Chuck supports initiatives focused on advocacy, organizational growth, awareness, and strengthening support networks for current and former Submariners. His dedication reflects SAG’s core values of integrity, professionalism, and service to the Silent Service community.
Chuck remains committed to supporting fellow Submariners and helping ensure their service, sacrifices, and long-term health concerns continue to receive meaningful advocacy and recognition.

name: Dana Widmayer
bio: Dana Widmayer serves as the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) for the Submariners’ Advocacy Group (SAG), where he supports the organization’s financial stewardship, operational accountability, and long-term sustainability initiatives. In this role, he helps oversee financial planning, fiscal compliance, and organizational resource management in support of SAG’s mission to advocate for U.S. Navy Submariners, veterans, and their families.

A proud member of the Silent Service community, Dana previously served aboard USS LEWIS AND CLARK (SSBN 644), where he gained firsthand experience in the operational demands, discipline, and unique culture of submarine service. His connection to the Submarine Force continues to shape his commitment to supporting fellow Submariners and advocating for the long-term well-being of the undersea warfare community.

Throughout his professional career, Dana has built extensive experience in financial management, administrative operations, and organizational support. His background includes leadership in budgeting, financial oversight, reporting, and business operations, bringing both precision and professionalism to the nonprofit sector.

As part of SAG’s executive leadership team, Dana plays an important role in supporting the organization’s continued growth and development as it expands its advocacy efforts, member services, outreach initiatives, and national visibility. His commitment to accountability, professionalism, and mission-focused service helps strengthen SAG’s ability to support the Submarine community and advocate for issues affecting current and former Submariners.

Dana’s dedication to supporting the Submarine Force community reflects SAG’s core values of integrity, professionalism, and service. Through his work behind the scenes, he contributes to the organizational foundation necessary to sustain effective advocacy and long-term impact for the Silent Service community.

name: Jerry Lainhart
bio: Jerry D. Lainhart serves on the Board of Directors for the Submariners’ Advocacy Group (SAG), supporting the organization’s mission to advocate for U.S. Navy Submariners, veterans, and their families. A qualified Submariner and proud member of the Silent Service community, Jerry brings operational submarine experience, professional leadership, and a lifelong commitment to service to SAG’s growing national advocacy efforts.

Jerry qualified in submarines aboard USS CAVALLA (SSN 684) in March 1990 while serving as an Electronics Technician. During his assignment aboard CAVALLA from 1989 through 1993, he supported the demanding operational mission requirements associated with fast-attack submarine operations during a critical period in modern naval history. His time in the Submarine Force instilled the values of professionalism, accountability, teamwork, and mission-focused service that continue to guide him today.

Following his naval service, Jerry pursued higher education and professional development, earning a Bachelor of Science degree from Brigham Young University in 1999 and a Master of Science degree from the University of Wisconsin–Platteville in 2005. He later achieved certification as a Project Management Professional (PMP), further strengthening his leadership and organizational management expertise.

Jerry’s combined background in submarine operations, technical systems, higher education, and project management provides valuable perspective in support of SAG’s mission and organizational growth. His experience reflects a continued commitment to professional excellence, disciplined leadership, and supporting fellow members of the Submarine community.

As part of SAG’s leadership team, Jerry supports initiatives focused on advocacy, awareness, and strengthening support networks for current and former Submariners. His dedication reflects SAG’s core values of integrity, professionalism, and service to the Silent Service community.
Jerry currently resides in Thayne, Wyoming, with his wife, LaDawna.

name: Patrick Ivory
bio: Patrick Ivory serves in a leadership role within the Submariners’ Advocacy Group (SAG), supporting the organization’s mission to advocate for U.S. Navy Submariners, veterans, and their families. A proud member of the Silent Service community, Patrick brings decades of submarine experience, operational leadership, and continued dedication to supporting those who have served beneath the sea.

Throughout his naval career, Patrick served aboard multiple U.S. Navy submarines, gaining firsthand experience in the demanding operational environment, discipline, and unique brotherhood associated with undersea warfare. His service within the Submarine Force provided extensive leadership experience while reinforcing the values of accountability, professionalism, teamwork, and mission accomplishment that continue to guide his work today.

Over the course of his distinguished submarine career, Patrick supported critical operational missions and contributed to the readiness and effectiveness of the crews and commands with which he served. His experiences in the Silent Service established a lifelong commitment to supporting fellow Submariners and advocating for the recognition and support they deserve long after their military service concludes.

Following his military career, Patrick continued to build upon his leadership and professional experience through work focused on operational support, organizational collaboration, and community engagement. His ability to connect with others, remain mission-focused, and support organizational growth has made him a valued contributor within both professional and veteran-service environments.

Within SAG, Patrick supports initiatives designed to strengthen advocacy efforts, expand organizational outreach, and increase awareness surrounding the long-term impacts associated with submarine service. His commitment to service reflects SAG’s core values of integrity, professionalism, and dedication to the Silent Service community.

Patrick remains committed to ensuring that current and former Submariners, as well as their families, continue to receive meaningful advocacy, support, and recognition for their sacrifices and contributions to national defense.

name: Bruce Tarleton
bio: Bruce Tarleton is a founding member of the Submariners’ Advocacy Group (SAG) and serves as a leading voice in the organization’s mission to advocate for U.S. Navy Submariners, veterans, and their families. A proud member of the Silent Service community, Bruce has dedicated himself to increasing awareness surrounding the long-term health impacts and unseen hazards associated with submarine service.

Throughout his naval career, Bruce served in the United States Navy Submarine Force, where he gained firsthand experience operating within the demanding and highly disciplined environment unique to undersea warfare. His service in the Silent Service instilled the values of professionalism, accountability, resilience, and mission-focused teamwork that continue to guide his advocacy efforts today.

Bruce’s personal experiences following his submarine service became a driving force behind his commitment to supporting fellow Submariners and raising awareness surrounding the long-term health concerns affecting the undersea warfare community. Recognizing the need for stronger advocacy, improved awareness, and increased support for those exposed to the unique environmental conditions associated with submarine operations, he became one of the driving forces behind the formation and growth of SAG.

As a founding member of SAG, Bruce has helped support organizational outreach, veteran engagement, awareness initiatives, and advocacy efforts focused on ensuring the experiences and sacrifices of Submariners receive the attention and recognition they deserve. His continued dedication reflects SAG’s core values of integrity, professionalism, and service to the Silent Service community.

Bruce remains committed to supporting current and former Submariners while helping advance national awareness regarding the long-term health and exposure concerns associated with life beneath the sea.
